title: Is a structured interview stage worth it? (Brogden utility as value of information)
story: Andrew's 'Pricing an interview' calculation. The current process predicts performance with validity 0.25; adding a structured interview adds about 0.10 to the composite (here a range, 0.03 to 0.20). Output is worth GBP 16k per SD, one hire per five shortlisted (zbar(0.2) = 1.40 SD above the pool mean) and four years of tenure. Four candidates are interviewed per hire, each interview costing about GBP 600 of internal time (range 200 to 3,000).
source: Marritt, 'Should you replace Sam?', section 'Pricing an interview'
what_it_tests: formulas with zbar() and numbers defined by formulas of other numbers
the article's ~GBP 9,000 per hire and ~GBP 2,200 per-interview break-even
the ceiling: a perfect predictor is worth ~GBP 67,000 per hire
